name: SD-RAN RAN Simulator
what_it_is: A simulator for RAN CU/DU nodes and RU cells from ONF's SD-RAN project that communicates over the O-RAN E2AP standard. It creates virtual gNodeB (gNB) environments for testing xApps and E2 termination points without physical radio hardware.
components: ran-simulator (core simulation engine for CU/DU nodes and RU cells)
onos-e2t (E2 termination point — receives E2AP messages from simulated nodes)
onos-e2sub (E2 subscription service — manages service model subscriptions)
onos-cli (CLI for runtime control via `onos-cli ransim` commands)
YAML topology model loader (defines simulated environment at startup)
gRPC API (enables dynamic environment changes at runtime)
protocols: O-RAN E2AP (primary protocol between simulated gNBs and onos-e2t)
SCTP (transport layer for E2AP connections to onos-e2t endpoint)
gRPC (internal API for runtime control and dynamic scenario changes)
measurement: KPM (Key Performance Measurement) service model — periodic UE/cell metrics reports
PCI (Physical Cell Identity) values generated per cell
RC (Radio Control) service model — control-loop interactions
configuration: YAML topology model file loaded at startup (defines node count, cell layout, neighbor relations)
gNodeB type set to G_NB for E2 node registration
Runtime modifications via gRPC API (change topology/metrics without restart)
modes: Integrated SD-RAN mode (full stack with onos-e2t, onos-e2sub, onos-topo)
Standalone simulation mode (load YAML model, expose gRPC API only)
Dynamic scenario mode (runtime gRPC calls mutate topology/metrics mid-run)
constraints: Released source code (v1.1.1 snapshot) cannot build functional binaries — depends on private ONF repositories
Active development branches require ONF membership access
Requires a running Kubernetes cluster and Helm 3.0+ for deployment (no bare-metal docker-compose path documented)
No fault injection or failure scenario modeling documented
Read-only open-source mirror — no pull requests accepted upstream
notable_absences: No docker-compose file — Kubernetes/Helm is the only supported deployment method
No fault injection or node failure simulation capability
No performance benchmarking or load-generation tooling
No multi-tenancy or isolation features documented
No RRC/NAS layer simulation (E2AP only, no full protocol stack)
